To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the best method for the determination of trace elements in inorganic samples is to use the method of choice for the determination of the element, and then to add the sample to the standard solution.

the use of a single method for the determination of a given element in a wide variety of materials is not feasible and that the choice of a suitable method must be based on a knowledge of the nature of the sample.

the most important parameters in the determination of elements at the trace and ultra-trace level in inorganic and biological matrices are: (i) the sample size, (ii) the method for sample preparation and dissolution, (iii) the separation technique, and (iv) the method of detection.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problems: (i) the preparation and dissolution in acid solutions of solid samples of organic and inorganic origin, (ii) the separation of elements from the solution of the samples and their pre-concentration in the form of a precipitate, a complex or a chelate, and (iii) the separation and pre-concentration of elements by liquid-liquid extraction.

the development of methods for the determination of elements at the ppb or ppM levels in inorganic and biological materials, with particular reference to the determination of trace elements in biological fluids.
the development of methods for the determination of the elements in the ppb range, and with their application to problems in environmental chemistry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in general, solution techniques are not the best way of preparing samples for trace determination.
, although solution techniques have been used with success for many years, they are still in a state of flux and that the methods are still far from being fully satisfactory.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
solution techniques are useful, but that they are not a panacea for all problems of trace analysis.

, in the determination of elements at trace and ultra-trace levels, the direct determination of the element in the sample matrix is to be preferred to the indirect determination of the element after separation and concentration.
the errors in solution methods are not significantly greater, and in many cases they are less, than the errors associated with direct methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a single method is unlikely to be successful.

the sample preparation and separation techniques used for the determination of trace elements in inorganic samples are also applicable to the determination of trace organic compounds in inorganic and biological samples.
there is a need for more research into the preparation, dissolution and separation of trace elements in samples of biological, environmental, geological and technological origin.
